key_insight: A 20-qubit trapped-ion QPU can supply expectation values for NLCE+QA that reconstruct thermodynamic-limit ground-state energies and a quasi-particle dispersion, but only if classical post-processing remains numerically stable.
engineering_relevance: This shows how near-term quantum hardware could be used as a subroutine for scalable materials and condensed-matter calculations that extrapolate from small clusters to infinite systems.
method: NLCE+QA to extract thermodynamic-limit observables from small-cluster computations
PCAT-style projector-based block diagonalization for energies and dispersion relations
CX-test readout on the QPU, with ASP and VQE as state-preparation approaches
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results for TFIM and related 1D/ladder settings, comparing QPU-derived expectation values under adiabatic state preparation and classical-trained VQE to assess whether they survive noise-sensitive nonlinear post-processing.
watch_item: Matrix inversion and square-root steps in PCAT can amplify measurement noise, so hardware readout precision is a key bottleneck before the approach can outperform classical methods.
paper_title: Thermodynamic-limit dispersion relations on trapped-ion quantum hardware
